The exact determinant det(zI-T)=z^20(z^2-z+1)(z^5-z+1) and explicit 7..24 integer traces are replayed from the embedded 27-state SymPy script. Exact rational isolation certifies one negative real quintic root smaller than -7/6, four other quintic roots of modulus <11/10, and strict dominance from order 25; an independently implemented signed-graph deletion recursion confirms 7..14. No assumption of an infinite proof from finite sampling, no equality asserted between index and degeneracy.

value.rationale: The all-size nonvanishing index guarantees at least one exact supersymmetric zero mode for every simple GP(n,3). The unique dominant negative transfer root forces at least exponentially many ground states at rate log(rho)/2 per graph vertex, a nontrivial protected degeneracy across an infinite natural cubic family. Witten lower bounds can cancel or vanish for other networks; generic transfer technology, a finite table and a single-order computation do not settle this exact sign and rate theorem.
